heading: INT. BOMBED CATHEDRAL - ORGAN LOFT - DUSK

units.text: INT. BOMBED CATHEDRAL - ORGAN LOFT - DUSK
Half the nave is open to the sky.
The great organ pipes hang bent and blackened like the ribs of a burned animal.
Plaster dust drifts through the last light, and somewhere below, water drips from a broken font.
Behind a carved screen on the loft, the stairs to the nave have collapsed into rubble.
SERGEANT TAVARES (30s, sapper's gloves, a rifle he has stopped trusting) crawls onto the loft on his stomach, dragging a pack that clinks with wire and blasting cord.
He freezes.

A boy in a grey uniform, a STRANGER (teens, hollow cheeks, a cracked helmet twice his size), sits against the base of the organ console with a service pistol in both hands, aimed at Tavares's forehead, trembling.
They stare at each other across ten feet of splintered oak.
Easy. Easy now.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: You stop. I shoot.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: I've stopped. See?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: He flattens his palms on the floor.
The Stranger doesn't lower the pistol.
A bell somewhere in the tower sounds once, thin and cracked, answering the wind.
You're hurt.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: The Stranger glances at his left leg.
Blood has soaked through the trouser and dried black to the knee.
He looks back up and shrugs with the exaggerated carelessness of someone who is very afraid.
It is nothing.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: It's something. It's a lot of something.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: The Stranger swallows.
The pistol wavers, steadies.
Tavares breathes out slowly through his nose and lets his shoulders drop an inch, an invitation, a language older than either of their armies.
My name is Tavares. Mateus Tavares.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: I do not want your name.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Then you can give me yours later.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Silence.
The wind finds a pipe and moans through it, a single hollow note.
The Stranger flinches.
The pistol dips toward the floor and snaps up again.
That's the wind. Just the wind.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: The Stranger nods, wet-eyed.
Tavares slides one hand to his pack and loosens the strap with two fingers.
Very slowly he pulls out a flat tin, thumbs it open, and sets it on the floor halfway between them.
Hard biscuit.
A cube of chocolate wrapped in wax paper.
Eat.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: The Stranger doesn't move.
His stomach growls loud in the hush of the loft.
He winces.
Tavares smiles faintly and slides the tin an inch closer with his boot.
No trick. If I wanted you dead, I'd have let the stairs do it.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Lukas.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Sorry?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: My name. Lukas.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Tavares nods as though a contract has been signed.
He lowers himself to sit, back against a pillar, a calm arm's length away from the tin.
Lukas reaches for the biscuit with his left hand, never lowering the pistol in his right.
He bites.
Chews.
His eyes close for one second, an animal relief.
Good?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: It is stale.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: It's army.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Lukas almost laughs.
The pistol sinks to his lap at last.
For a while neither of them speaks.
The light goes amber, then rust.
The wind rises, and the broken pipes take up a long sigh.
You are here to blow up the church.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: I'm here to blow up the tower. The church is already blown up.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: My brother is in the tower.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Tavares goes still.
He studies the boy.
Your brother?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: He is the observer. He spots for the guns. I come to bring him water and the bell wire is cut and the stairs are... (gestures at the rubble) ...and then you.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: How old is he?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Twenty-two.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Tavares pulls a canteen from his belt.
He unscrews it and holds it out across the gap.
Lukas hesitates, then takes it, and drinks like a man who has forgotten how.
Does he have a radio up there?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Yes.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Could he hear you if you shouted?
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: If I shouted loud.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Tavares lifts his charges from the pack, one by one, and lays them on the floor in a row.
Then, with a deliberate slowness, he cuts the fuse on each, a clean snip, and drops the lengths of cord into the dark under the console.
Tell him the sergeant says come down. Tell him nobody's firing. Tell him the sun's going.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Lukas stares at the cut fuses.
You will be punished.
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Probably.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Why?
units.name: LUKAS

units.text: Tavares looks up at the shattered clerestory, at the first star pricking through.
Because I've got a brother too.
units.name: TAVARES

units.text: Lukas stands, gripping the console for balance.
He cups his hands around his mouth and shouts something in his own language up the long throat of the tower, a name, and then a word that means come.
The echo comes back down, thin, unanswered.
They wait.
The first star becomes two.
Finally, from far above, a faint voice calls back.
Lukas turns to Tavares, and for the first time the boy is a boy, grinning, tears on his dirty face.
Tavares leans his head against the stone pillar and closes his eyes.
